analysis:
The supplied units are head-side excerpts of CHANGELOG.md lines 806-1243, and the patch excerpt shows the only changed lines are 11-39 (a new v0.10.10 candidate section). Those changed lines fall outside the numbered excerpts I received, so I could not inspect them line by line. Both units are historical release notes for v0.10.6 through v0.10.9. Documentation changes do not alter runtime security behavior, so I found no security regression in what I examined.

Security-relevant claims in the notes, which later passes should check against code:
- The changelog states that the enabled-model filter now refuses coordinator load_model and prefetch_model for models outside it (relevant to A-004 and TB-002).
- It states that rollback is quarantined and follows a pair's partner (T-043, TB-003). The rollback is described as journaled, under the update lease, and checked for hash and signature.
- It describes Sandbox setup (TB-013, T-061) as downloading the installer and running it as the owner. It also says the CLI never passes the installer's --force.
- It describes the encrypted SSD prefix cache (T-041) as unchanged in kind. Gemma 4 and Qwen tensor-parallel prefix reuse is described as using the same encrypted SSD tier, with restoration only when both Macs hold the prefix.
- It says coordinator registration for cluster pairs depends on release-derived approvals (TB-002, TB-011). This is described as a platform-owned, out-of-scope backend contract.
- The patch excerpt says new sandbox setups and new pairs need account waitlist approval. It adds that waitlisted, unapproved, or unreachable-coordinator states exit 1 and change nothing. It also says the sandbox --yes flag adds the account to the waitlist without asking, and that the cluster local path stays offline. The excerpt is truncated, and I cannot see how the coordinator fallback works when it does not offer waitlists ("both new setups go on as in 0..."). If the coordinator not offering waitlists lets setup proceed, that could be a client-side gate bypass for the waitlist approval. It is policy rather than a security boundary and is not verifiable from the supplied evidence.

No code was supplied, so none of these behaviors could be verified. I did not see the full new v0.10.10 section, and this does not amount to a full audit. A reviewer with the real code diff should confirm the waitlist gate's fail-open versus fail-closed behavior.
